author: Swinhoe, 1863
summary: 우리나라에서는 북부의 평안도 지역에 사는 작은 새로, 흔하지만 재빠르고 겁이 많아 사람 눈에 잘 띄지 않는다. 봄에는 작은 무리를 지어 나뭇가지 사이를 옮겨 다니며 곤충을 잡는데, 주로 딱정벌레류와 나비류의 애벌레와 어른벌레를 먹는다. 아무르 동부, 하바롭스크, 우수리 남부, 만주 동부 등지에서 번식하고 인도차이나, 캄보디아, 미얀마 동부 등지에서 겨울을 나며, 중국 동부·중부와 만주 등을 거쳐 이동한다.

art.subject: Chestnut-flanked White-eye (Zosterops erythropleurus), adult (sexes alike), as seen in Korea on migration in May and September: crown, nape, back, wings and tail yellowish olive-green; black lores; broad, complete white eye-ring; chin and throat bright yellow; breast greyish-white, darker and almost grey on the breast sides; belly white; a large chestnut patch on the flanks below the folded wing (its size varies between birds); undertail coverts yellow. Bill thin, pointed and very slightly decurved, dull grey with a paler base to the lower mandible; iris brown; legs dull grey.
art.pose: moving quickly along a twig, picking insects from the foliage
art.scene: Korean migration season in May: deciduous woodland edge and canopy with fresh green leaves; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a twig: yellowish olive-green upperparts, black lores, broad white eye-ring, bright yellow chin and throat, greyish-white breast with greyer sides, white belly, large chestnut flank patch, grey legs
adult, front view perched: bright yellow throat ending sharply above a greyish-white breast with greyer sides, chestnut flank patches on both sides, yellow undertail coverts
art.build: Tiny, slim, very active songbird, about 10.5cm, smaller than a sparrow. Rounded head, short neck. Bill fine and pointed, shorter than the head, very slightly curved. Legs short, grey. Moves quickly through twigs and foliage, often hanging upside down to glean insects, and travels in small restless flocks. At rest the wingtips reach a short way past the base of the tail. Tail short to medium, square-ended, olive-green.
avoid: Do not paint the flanks buff or brownish without a clear chestnut patch; that is Warbling (Japanese) White-eye.
Do not make the whole underparts yellow; only the chin, throat and undertail coverts are yellow.
Do not paint a thin, broken or coloured eye-ring; it is a broad, complete white ring.
Do not give it a thick finch-like bill.
